html:
The Sekakawon, also written Chicacoan, were a small Algonquian-speaking people of the Northern Neck of Virginia, between the Potomac and Rappahannock rivers near the Chesapeake Bay. They appear on John Smith's map of 1612.

They were part of the paramount chiefdom of Powhatan or close to it, and their neighbours included the Patawomeck and Cuttatawomen. English settlers took up the Northern Neck from the 1640s, and the Sekakawon merged with other small groups there.
